skills.name: The circumscribed circle of a triangle

note.text:
The circumscribed circle of a triangle passes through its three vertices. Its centre O is where the three perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet (the circumcentre): O is the same distance from A, B and C.
To draw it: draw two perpendicular bisectors; where they cross is O; the radius is OA.
In a right-angled triangle, the centre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, and the radius is half the hypotenuse.
Example: a right-angled triangle with sides 6, 8, 10 cm has a circumscribed circle of radius 5 cm.

worked_example.problem: A right-angled triangle has sides {a} cm and {b} cm next to the right angle. Find the radius of its circumscribed circle.
steps: The centre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse: radius = {c} ÷ {2} = {c / 2} cm.

cards.idea: The circumcentre is where the perpendicular bisectors meet.
example: It is the same distance from the three vertices.

misconceptions.explain: That is the diameter (the hypotenuse). Halve it.
The diameter is the hypotenuse, not a shorter side.

pick.q: Where is the centre of the circumscribed circle of a triangle?
pick.r: where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet
e: That is the centre of the inscribed circle.
pick.y: Every point of a perpendicular bisector is the same distance from both ends of the side.

pick.q: Where is the centre of the circumscribed circle of a right-angled triangle?
pick.r: at the midpoint of the hypotenuse
w: at the midpoint of the shortest side
e: The right-angle vertex is on the circle.
For a right-angled triangle it is on the hypotenuse.
It is the midpoint of the longest side.
pick.y: The hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of {c} cm. Find the radius of its circumscribed circle.

misconceptions.explain: The hypotenuse is the diameter; the radius is half of it.

misconceptions.explain: That is the diameter (the hypotenuse). Halve it.

right.text: The circumscribed circle passes through the three vertices.
The circumcentre is the same distance from A, B and C.
In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumscribed circle.
Two perpendicular bisectors are enough to find the circumcentre.

wrong.text: The circumcentre is always inside the triangle.
wrong.explain: For an obtuse triangle it is outside; for a right-angled one it is on the hypotenuse.

wrong.text: The circumcentre is where the medians meet.
wrong.explain: The medians meet at the centroid.
